source.title: RabbitMQ node: queue bindings aren't awaited before the channel is returned

source.body:
### Bug Description

This happens at line 80 in packages/nodes-base/nodes/RabbitMQ/GenericFunctions.ts. forEach in options.binding.bindings.forEach(async (binding) => { ... bindQueue ... }) doesn't wait for the async callbacks. As a result, it returns the channel before bindQueue has finished, so messages that arrive right after can be missed. Also, if a bind fails, the error isn't caught by the surrounding try/catch. To fix: await each bind in a for...of loop, or use Promise.all.

### To Reproduce

1.Create a workflow using the RabbitMQ node or the RabbitMQ Trigger.

2.In the options, choose an exchange and add at least two bindings.

3. To see the failure case, set one binding to an exchange that doesn't exist.

4.Run the workflow.

5. Result: the logs show an error that the surrounding try/catch didn't handle. If all bindings use existing exchanges, messages that arrive right after the start can be missed.

6. I found this bug by reading the code with my open source tool. I haven't reproduced it myself.

### Expected behavior

The node should return the channel only after every binding has finished.
If a binding fails, it should show up as a node error.

### Debug Info

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: Confirmed in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/RabbitMQ/GenericFunctions.ts`: `rabbitmqConnectQueue()` uses `forEach(async ...)` and then immediately resolves the outer promise. The bind promises are therefore neither awaited nor connected to that `try/catch`, so the caller can receive the channel before bindings finish and a rejected bind can escape the intended error path. `await Promise.all(options.binding.bindings.map(binding => channel.bindQueue(queue, binding.exchange, binding.routingKey)))` inside the existing `try` would wait for all binds and propagate a rejection.
